parts:
Hello!

I am new to using NIMBLE and am hoping to use it to implement the Cross Categorization (CrossCat) model defined in this paper: https://jmlr.org/papers/volume17/11-392/11-392.pdf

The model involves simultaneously clustering tabular data by both rows and columns using two separate chinese restaurant processes. I am using version 1.2.1 of NIMBLE in RStudio on a Mac. Below is my attempt at writing NIMBLE code to fit this model:

library(nimble)
library(LaplacesDemon)

fake_data <- data.frame(response_id=1:170)
for(q in 1:120) {
  fake_data[,paste("Q", q, sep="")] <- sample(1:7, 170, replace = TRUE)
}

setAlphas <- nimbleFunction(run=function() {
  returnType(double(1, 7))
  alphas <- c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
  return(alphas)
})
code <- nimbleCode({
  z[1:N] ~ dCRP(alpha1, size = N)
  alpha1 ~ dgamma(1, 1)
  y[1:Q] ~ dCRP(alpha2, size = Q)
  alpha2 ~ dgamma(1, 1)
 
  alphas[1:7] <- setAlphas()
  for(i in 1:M) {
    for(j in 1:R) {
      thetas[i, j, 1:7] ~ ddirch(alphas[1:7])
    }
  }
 
  for(i in 1:N) {
    r[i, 1] <- i
    for(j in 1:Q) {
      z_thetas[1:R, 1:7] <- thetas[z[i], 1:R, 1:7]
      y_thetas[1:7] <- z_thetas[y[i], 1:7]
      r[i, (j+1)] ~ dcat(y_thetas[1:7])
    }
  }
})

set.seed(1)
constants <- list(N = 169, M = 10, Q = 117, R = 10)
data <- list(r=fake_data)
init_thetas <- array(dim=c(constants$M, constants$R, 7))
for(i in 1:constants$M) {
  for(j in 1:constants$R) {
    init_thetas[i, j, 1:7] <- rdirichlet(1, c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1))
  }
}
inits <- list(thetas = init_thetas,
              z = sample(1:10, size = constants$N, replace = TRUE),
              y = sample(1:10, size = constants$Q, replace = TRUE),
              alpha1  = 1, alpha2 = 1)
model <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)

# cmodel <- compileNimble(model)

monitors <- c('z', 'y')
nimbleOptions(MCMCusePredictiveDependenciesInCalculations = TRUE)
modelConf <- configureMCMC(model, print=TRUE, useConjugacy=FALSE, monitors = monitors)
modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)

cmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = model)
cmodelMCMC$run(1000)

samples <- as.matrix(cmodelMCMC$mvSamples)

However, when I get to the buildMCMC step, I get the following error: 

sampler_CRP: The number of nodes that are jointly clustered must be the same for each group. For example if 'mu[i,j]' are clustered such that all nodes for a given 'i' must be in the same cluster, then the number of nodes for each 'i' must be the same. Group 1 has 19773 nodes being clustered where 117 are expected.

Does this mean that the kind of joint CRP structure that is necessary for the CrossCat model is not currently available in NIMBLE? Is there another way I could write this model that would work with the current version?

Thanks in advance for your help!

Hi Thomas,

I haven't had time to look too deeply at this, but one initial thing that I see is that in the block of code below, the first two lines don't have `j` in them.  That leads to this warning:

```

Defining model

  [Warning] Multiple definitions for the same node.

            Did you forget indexing with 'i,j' on the left-hand side of

            `z_thetas[1:10, 1:7] <- thetas[z[i], 1:10, 1:7]`?

  [Warning] Multiple definitions for the same node.

            Did you forget indexing with 'i,j' on the left-hand side of

            `y_thetas[1:7] <- z_thetas[y[i], 1:7]`?

```


As a first step, could you rework your model so that you are not redefining the same node multiple times (i.e., defining `z_thetas[1:4, 1:7]` Q different times and similarly for `y_thetas[1:7]`). Once you've addressed that, let us know what happens in terms of the MCMC set up.

Also, these are minor side comments, but you don't need `setAlphas`. You can just set `alphas` via `constants` (or, it's also possible to do `alphas[1:7] <- rep(1,7)` though it's unnecessary here). And you don't need in the code to set `r[i, 1] <- i` . Just set that row of `r` via `data`.

parts:
Thanks, Thomas.

So, this model structure falls in a grey zone for our CRP sampling. Back when we had funding support for a researcher to work on implementing the CRP, we talked about handling this case, but we never quite got it all done.  I believe the error message you are getting is an overly cautious one. And that we could disable it and NIMBLE could do the sampling. However, it might not mix very well because it would not use conjugacy in sampling the new cluster memberships even if the conjugacy was present. (Working on that was what we hoped to do but did not have time to do.) Basically, when the sampling proposes a new cluster, it would use a 'nonconjugate' sampler that proposes new cluster parameters from their prior, rather than determining whether to open a new cluster based on the marginal probability (marginalizing over possible cluster parameter values) and then when opening a new cluster, determining the new cluster parameters by drawing from the conditional distribution given prior and data. 

If you'd like to try it out with the nonconjugate approach, I could set you up with a branch of nimble that you could install from and you could experiment to see how well it works for your problem.

-chris
